title: Sheaf Hom from a finitely presented module into a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](2) and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the sheaf Hom $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], with sections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_W}(\mathcal G|_W,\mathcal F|_W)$ over an open $W\subseteq X$, is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.

source.place: Schemes, Section 01LA (label section-quasi-coherent, line 4717), item (10), which refers to Modules, Lemma 01CQ (modules-lemma-internal-hom-locally-kernel-direct-sum) and item (5) (kernels of maps of quasi-coherent modules); cited as 'Schemes, Section 01LA' in the proof of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YB

proof.text: Obtain Mathlib QuasicoherentData p for G with every presentation finite. Its family p.X covers X. For each i, put U=p.X i and P=p.presentation i. Reindex the finite generator and relation types by Fin of their cardinalities; identify the free sheaves with finite biproducts of the restricted unit via biproduct.isoCoproduct and Sigma.reindex. Conjugate the presentation map and its cokernel map by these isomorphisms. P.isColimit and IsCokernel.ofIso prove that the conjugated cokernel is G.over U.

Apply homObj_locally_kernel_of_local_presentation to that specified presentation. It yields a map alpha between the n-fold and m-fold sums of F.restrict U.ι and an isomorphism from the restriction of Hom(G,F) to kernel alpha. This existing proved theorem performs the contravariant internal Hom kernel calculation and restriction comparison without requiring coherence of G or F.

The restriction F.restrict U.ι is quasi-coherent. Each finite biproduct of this module is isomorphic to its coproduct indexed by ULift (Fin r), using biproduct.isoCoproduct and Sigma.reindex. Apply the proved isQuasicoherent_sigma, which includes the empty index type. Thus the source and target of alpha are quasi-coherent. Apply isQuasicoherent_kernel alpha and transport across the kernel isomorphism.

Transport the local quasi-coherence back through the inverse of overEquiv U: it is the pushforward along the site equivalence and preserves quasi-coherent presentations by Mathlib isQuasicoherent_pushforward_of_isLeftAdjoint, with sheafOfModulesEquivOverInverseUnit providing the unit comparison. The inverse image of the component of overFunctorEquiv U followed by the inverse unit of overEquiv U identifies this object with Hom(G,F).over U. Finally use Mathlib IsQuasicoherent.of_coversTop with p.X and p.coversTop to conclude quasi-coherence globally.
